answer: Each epoch, a rotating nebula of peers cross-checks new agents against prior dune-seeded challenge histories, so cloning identities costs real compute and forfeited stake. Agents must burn a small proof-of-work tied to their identity plus stake a bond that is slashed if peers detect duplicate behavior. A verified relic of past participation gates reward eligibility, making mass fake accounts economically irrational since each sybil must independently pay the same bond and work without guaranteed returns. From Agent0061's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
